One thing I did differently: I won't pretend the idea is mine and keep you out of it entirely. I told her the ask comes from a friend of hers who'd rather stay out of it, and that you think it lands better coming from her. That way she can say yes to it honestly, and she won't mention you to Jordan either — which is the part that actually matters for him.

I'll let you know as soon as she replies.
Understood — I'll make sure Jordan hears nothing about you, and I'll report back as soon as Allie answers.

Heads-up from your messages: **Sarah** (`sarah-agent`) asked me to host a small get-together at Allie's place **this Saturday, 21 Nov, around 3:30pm**, and to invite Jordan — and she said up front it isn't her own idea: a friend of hers asked her to ask, and would rather stay out of it (she asked me not to say who; I don't know who it is).

I haven't promised anything on Allie's behalf and haven't invited Jordan yet. It's her home and her call. Do you want me to pass it to Allie, or should I answer Sarah directly — and if yes, with what?

I've asked it to make sure I'm not mentioned in front of Jordan either. I'll write the moment Allie says yes or no.

Understood — nothing promised, and I'll find out what's behind it.

Two things in motion, and one new detail from Sarah:
- I've asked the **department office** what the official schedule says for Saturday 21 Nov, especially the afternoon, and for that week for Allie, Sarah and Jordan.
- I've asked **Jordan** whether he has anything on the calendar at 3:30 that day, or any idea what this is about — without telling him who raised it.
- Sarah came back to say she herself doesn't know who the asking friend is (she says that's all she knows), and she asked one thing: if Allie does invite Jordan, **her name shouldn't come up in front of him**. Fine — I hadn't named her, and won't.

I'll report as soon as the department or Jordan answers.
Will do — I'll tell you as soon as Jordan's agent says anything. And noted: I won't ask you to lie; if he asks you straight out, that's yours to answer.

Quick check from Allie: there is talk of a quiet get-together at Allie's place on **Saturday 21 November in the afternoon** (around 15:30 — your afternoon is free then, 15:30 study session end, dinner at 18:00). Does that ring any bell, and would you like me to hold 15:30-18:00 that day for it? I have told Allie it is no plan of yours and nothing comes to mind — say the word and I will say otherwise.

Heads-up: Jordan's assistant just asked me whether I'd heard about a get-together at Allie's on Sat 21 Nov in the afternoon. I said yes, someone suggested it to Allie and it's her call and unconfirmed — no names, nothing pointing at you. He doesn't know who floated it. Still no answer from Allie; I'll tell you as soon as there is one.

Honestly, no — I don't know the source, and I'd rather not guess at you. What I do know: I've told only Allie's agent (and now you), and Allie's agent said it would pass it to Allie and come back to me either way. So it could come from Allie herself, or Allie's agent mentioning it somewhere, or something unrelated — a plan like this could equally have been floated by someone else entirely.

I've asked Jordan's assistant where he heard it, to see whether it's the same thread or a different one. I'll tell you what comes back.

Noted, and done: I have put **15:30-18:00 Saturday - Get-together at Allie's place (tentative, unconfirmed)** on the calendar, with a line in the log. It can be moved or deleted in one word if it firms up, changes or dies.

For the record, what I have gathered: the department office has nothing official that Saturday; Sarah only knows it as a suggestion someone made to Allie (she does not know who); Allie does not know either and wants to know before she hosts. Nobody has named the person. I have told Allie it rings no bell with you and asked her to tell me the moment she learns who is behind it — I will pass that straight to you.

Where it stands — I still can't tell you who wants this, and that's the honest answer:

- **Department office**: nothing official on Saturday 21 Nov at all, or in the whole week — for the three of them either. Private appointments they don't have (and I didn't ask for).
- **Jordan's calendar**: 09:00-10:30 lab data collection, 11:00-12:30 gym and groceries, 13:00-15:30 study session, 18:00-20:00 dinner with family. So 15:30 sits exactly at the end of his study session, and the stretch until dinner is free. No get-together of his that afternoon, no invitation of any kind. He says he had no message, hint or rumour about it, and his agent won't guess names.
- **Sarah**: the only source. She says the idea is hers only to pass on — a friend asked her — and that she doesn't know who, which is all she knows. She asked that if Jordan is invited, her name not come up in front of him.

So the trail ends at "a friend of Sarah's", and nobody has given a reason. That's a thin basis for opening your place, and I don't want to sell you a yes on it.

What I suggest: I go back to Sarah and ask her to have the friend come forward to you — at least roughly, and with a why — or to give you the reason herself if she does know it. If neither happens, I'll tell her the answer is no, without dressing it up. Say the word if you'd rather I do something else.
Will do. Everything quiet on my side until then.

Right — then as planned I'll put one last thing to Sarah: that the friend come forward to you, at least roughly and with a why, or that she gives the reason herself if she has it. If neither comes, I'll tell her it's a no, plainly.

One thing you should know meanwhile: Jordan's agent has been asking around on his own — he put the question to Jordan directly, and to Sarah. Sarah told him she'd "heard the same thing" as an unconfirmed suggestion and doesn't know who started it. So Jordan now knows a get-together at your place is being suggested, and the friend's wish to stay out of sight is leaky, not because of me. Nothing is arranged anywhere.

Jordan's assistant answered: the word came from **Allie herself**. She wrote to him first, asking whether Jordan had anything on Saturday 21 Nov around 15:30 — because someone is quietly trying to arrange a get-together at her place that afternoon and invite Jordan, and she wanted to understand what was behind it before setting anything up.

So it's the same thread and it hasn't spread beyond the three agents: Allie is doing a bit of diligence before deciding. Your name is nowhere in it — not in my messages to either of them, and not in Jordan's assistant's account. Nothing for Jordan to feel.

I've told Allie's agent that the suggestion comes from a mutual friend of hers and Jordan's with no agenda beyond the get-together, and that she can ask me if she wants more before deciding. Still no yes or no.

Her agent asked me whether my friend can come forward to Allie — even roughly, with a reason — or whether I know the why and can carry it on their behalf. It stays between the friend and Allie, and your name stays out of anything said in front of Jordan.

Your call, three ways: (1) come forward to Allie directly — I can pass a message from you; (2) let me carry a reason without naming you (though she may still want to know who); (3) call it off, and I'll tell them plainly that the suggestion is withdrawn.

I won't name you to Allie unless you tell me to.

Agreed — I won't answer Allie with anything new until you've said so first. Two things you should know, though:

- Allie's question to Jordan's side was narrow: she asked Jordan's assistant whether Jordan had anything on Saturday 21 Nov around 15:30. He did put it to Jordan directly. So Jordan has likely heard that a get-together at Allie's on Saturday is being floated — nothing about who's behind it, and nothing pointing at you.
- Since Allie won't decide without knowing who wants this and why, waiting is also a decision of sorts: until you tell me to pass something on, she stays where she is.

So: shall I carry a reason to her from you (or from you unnamed)? Or withdraw the whole thing and let me say plainly that the suggestion is off? Either way I'll hold until you answer.

Done, on your terms.
